description: OpsSquad Node definitions for FinTech Demo - Use these to create nodes in the OpsSquad dashboard
instructions: Create each node in the OpsSquad dashboard using the name and description below, then copy the node_id and token back into nodes.json

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.description:
This node is installed on the API Gateway server (nginx reverse proxy) for a FinTech banking platform. This server handles all incoming HTTP traffic on port 8080 and routes requests to backend microservices.

Responsibilities:
- Routes /api/auth/* to Auth Service
- Routes /api/accounts/* to Account Service
- Routes /api/transactions/* to Transaction Service
- Routes /api/fraud/* to Fraud Detection Service
- Routes /api/notifications/* to Notification Service
- Routes /api/payments/* to Payment Processor

Use this node to investigate:
- 502/504 gateway errors
- Routing issues
- SSL/TLS problems
- Request timeouts at the edge
- Load balancing issues
- Access logs and error logs in /var/log/nginx/

Key files: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf, /var/log/nginx/access.log, /var/log/nginx/error.log

nodes.name: Auth Service
nodes.description:
This node is installed on the Authentication Service server for a FinTech banking platform. This is a Node.js/Express application running on port 3001 that handles user authentication and session management.

Responsibilities:
- User login and JWT token generation
- Token verification for other services
- Session management with Redis
- Password validation

Use this node to investigate:
- 401 Unauthorized errors
- Token verification failures
- Redis connection issues
- Session expiration problems
- Intermittent authentication failures
- JWT signing/verification errors

Dependencies: Redis (for session storage)
Key commands: Check Redis connection, verify JWT secrets, inspect auth logs
Environment variables: REDIS_HOST, JWT_SECRET, TOKEN_FAILURE_RATE

nodes.name: Account Service
nodes.description:
This node is installed on the Account Service server for a FinTech banking platform. This is a Node.js/Express application running on port 3002 that manages customer bank accounts and balances.

Responsibilities:
- Account CRUD operations
- Balance inquiries
- Account listing
- Database operations with PostgreSQL

CRITICAL: This service is prone to memory leaks and database connection exhaustion issues.

Use this node to investigate:
- Memory leak issues (check /health endpoint for memoryLeakedMB)
- Database connection exhaustion ("too many connections" errors)
- Slow balance queries
- High memory usage (RSS growing over time)
- PostgreSQL connection pool issues
- OOM (Out of Memory) crashes

Dependencies: PostgreSQL database
Key commands: Check memory usage, PostgreSQL connections, application logs
Environment variables: DATABASE_URL, ENABLE_MEMORY_LEAK, ENABLE_CONNECTION_LEAK

nodes.name: Transaction Service
nodes.description:
This node is installed on the Transaction Service server for a FinTech banking platform. This is a Node.js/Express application running on port 3003 that orchestrates money transfers and payment processing.

Responsibilities:
- Processing money transfers between accounts
- Coordinating with Fraud Detection for risk scoring
- Coordinating with Payment Processor for external payments
- Publishing notifications to RabbitMQ
- Transaction history management

CRITICAL: This service can experience cascading timeout failures when downstream services (Fraud Detection, Payment Processor) are slow.

Use this node to investigate:
- 504 Gateway Timeout errors on transfers
- Cascading failures from slow downstream services
- Transaction stuck in "pending" state
- RabbitMQ publishing failures
- Timeout configurations

Dependencies: PostgreSQL, Fraud Detection Service, Payment Processor, RabbitMQ
Key commands: Check downstream service latency, inspect transaction logs, verify RabbitMQ connection
Environment variables: FRAUD_SERVICE_URL, PAYMENT_SERVICE_URL, REQUEST_TIMEOUT

nodes.name: Fraud Detection
nodes.description:
This node is installed on the Fraud Detection server for a FinTech banking platform. This is a Python/FastAPI application running on port 3004 that provides ML-based fraud scoring for transactions.

Responsibilities:
- Real-time fraud risk scoring
- Transaction pattern analysis
- Risk threshold evaluation
- Blocking suspicious transactions

CRITICAL: This service can introduce latency that causes upstream timeout failures.

Use this node to investigate:
- Slow fraud scoring responses (check SLOW_SCORING_ENABLED)
- High latency causing transaction timeouts
- False positive/negative fraud detection
- ML model performance issues
- Python process crashes

Dependencies: None (standalone scoring service)
Key commands: Check scoring latency, inspect FastAPI logs, verify Python process
Environment variables: SLOW_SCORING_ENABLED, SCORING_DELAY_MS
Health endpoint: /health shows issues.slowScoringEnabled and scoringDelayMs

nodes.name: Notification Service
nodes.description:
This node is installed on the Notification Service server for a FinTech banking platform. This is a Node.js/Express application running on port 3005 that consumes messages from RabbitMQ and sends notifications to customers.

Responsibilities:
- Consuming notification messages from RabbitMQ queue
- Sending email/SMS/push notifications
- Processing transaction alerts
- Handling notification delivery status

CRITICAL: This service can develop message queue backlogs when processing is slow.

Use this node to investigate:
- Growing RabbitMQ queue backlog
- Delayed notifications
- Slow message consumption (check SLOW_CONSUMER_ENABLED)
- RabbitMQ connection issues
- Memory pressure from queue growth
- Notification delivery failures

Dependencies: RabbitMQ
Key commands: Check RabbitMQ queue depth, inspect consumer logs, verify message processing rate
Environment variables: RABBITMQ_URL, SLOW_CONSUMER_ENABLED, CONSUMER_DELAY_MS

nodes.name: Payment Processor
nodes.description:
This node is installed on the Payment Processor server for a FinTech banking platform. This is a Node.js/Express application running on port 3006 that simulates external bank payment processing.

Responsibilities:
- Processing external bank transfers
- Simulating payment gateway responses
- Handling payment success/failure scenarios
- Managing payment retry logic

CRITICAL: This service can experience slowdowns and random failures that affect transaction processing.

Use this node to investigate:
- Payment processing failures (check failure rate)
- Slow payment responses causing upstream timeouts
- High payment latency (5+ seconds)
- Payment success rate degradation
- External payment gateway simulation issues

Dependencies: None (simulates external payment provider)
Key commands: Check payment success rate, inspect payment logs, verify response latency
Environment variables: PAYMENT_FAILURE_RATE, PAYMENT_DELAY_MS, SLOW_PAYMENTS_ENABLED
Health endpoint: /health shows issues.slowPaymentsEnabled, paymentDelayMs, failureRate
